newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - A STATE OF FLUX.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - A STATE OF FLUX.

text.p: More rumours about Minet and Sedgwick remind us that the insurance broking sector has far from finished with consolidation. Elsewhere, the life and reinsurance sectors are still very much dominated by acquisitions and talk of further industry restructuring.
Those looking for an end to consolidation, when the various insurance sectors reach a state of balance, will probably be disappointed.
Insurance, like most industries is in a constant state of flux. New companies, new ideas and new ways of doing business are emerging all the time to challenge the status quo.

Amid all the heated interest over which of the big players are going to merge, countless small new entrants come hopefully to market. Many fall by the wayside, but a few survive and eventually become the key players of the future.

All today's big insurers can trace their roots back to humble origins. Some have taken decades to reach the big time, while a few, like Direct Line, have revolutionised the market in a matter of years.

Yesterday, green insurance intermediary Naturesave announced that in its small way it was expanding into commercial insurance. Naturesave is not going to challenge existing insurers in the spectacularly fast way that Direct Line did.

However, Naturesave has survived the crucial start-up years which see off most new ideas. The company itself, or the concept of tying insurance more actively to the environment, could be a force to be reckoned with in the next century.
